text:
marta: Hey team — running into a compatibility mess when consuming the JS SDK in a Bun edge worker + Deno test harness. Imports resolve fine in Node but Bun throws: `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `./dist/index.cjs`. Anyone seen a similar import/exports handshake issue?
kevin: Yup. Bun is strict about conditional exports and prefers ESM entrypoints. Did you try using the ESM build (`index.mjs` or `package.json` "module")?
sam: Bun also rewrites imports in edge workers sometimes. If your package has both `exports` and `main`, Bun might pick the wrong path. Quick check: does your package.json have an `exports` map that points `"./*"` to CJS first?
marta: It has `"main": "dist/index.cjs"` and `"exports": { ".": { "node": "dist/index.cjs", "default": "dist/index.mjs" } }`. Node picks node->cjs, Bun seems to want default->mjs but still complains.
jen: Also check MIME/Content-Type on importmaps for the edge worker. Bun's loader refuses some extensionless imports when served with wrong headers in local dev.
kevin: Another gotcha — our SDK uses `globalThis.crypto.subtle` for key derivation; Deno and Bun expose `crypto` but subtle APIs differ. Deno uses WebCrypto but requires `--unstable` in some versions? Bun historically had `webcrypto` under `globalThis.crypto` but lacked `importKey` behavior. Could be the runtime crypto causing the failure to initialize auth.
sam: For fetch: Bun's fetch is closer to web fetch but missing streaming body type details. If the SDK tries `response.body.getReader()` it will fail. Consider falling back to `response.arrayBuffer()` when `getReader` undefined.
marta: Our auth layer retries on 401 and then re-auths; in Bun it immediately throws inside the fetch polyfill and never reaches retry handler. I think the SDK's retry wrapper assumes Node's `fetch` semantics.
jen: Workarounds we used in a sample app: 1) Force ESM entry by adding `"type": "module"` in the published package or shipping a tiny `index.js` that re-exports the mjs build. 2) Add runtime guards around webcrypto ops: `const subtle = globalThis.crypto?.subtle ?? (await import('node:crypto').then(m=>m.webcrypto.subtle))`. 3) Use a lightweight fetch-shim for Bun: `if (!globalThis.fetch || typeof globalThis.fetch !== 'function') globalThis.fetch = (await import('undici')).fetch` (only for Node) — and guard so Bun's native fetch stays.
kevin: For typings: TS consumers on Deno complain because `types` in package.json points at `dist/index.d.ts` which references `node:` imports. Deno doesn't accept `node:` prefix. We should ship a Deno-friendly types file or use conditional types in `types` exports.
sam: Another option: publish an extra entrypoint `deno` in `exports` with paths that replace `node:` prefixes and point to `dist/deno.mjs` and `dist/deno.d.ts`. Consumers can then `import SDK from '@redwood/sdk/deno'` or Deno's import maps can remap.
marta: Good idea. For immediate unblock, I patched my local node_modules: created `./node_modules/@redwood/sdk/deno.mjs` that re-exports from `../dist/index.mjs` and removed `node:` refs from `d.ts`. Works for Deno tests.
jen: Can we add a small note in the README about runtime quirks and a devex sample app `examples/edge-bun-deno/` that shows minimal polyfills + import map + recommended package.json layout? New users hit this during onboarding.
kevin: Agreed. Also file a tiny DX bug: when the SDK detects `globalThis.Bun`, it should switch to a Bun-safe codepath (no node: imports, relaxed fetch usage, crypto guards). That would reduce friction.
infra-bot: deploy-canary: pushed sample app `examples/edge-bun-deno` to the docs repo — run `./scripts/dev.sh` to try locally.
marta: Thanks — I'll try the sample and share a minimal repro. If anyone wants the quick patch I used I can paste it here.
kevin: Please do. small snippets are helpful. :thumbsup:
